description: The figure presents three pie charts comparing the distribution of four categories across difficulty levels labeled “easy,” “medium,” and a third chart at the right (label not fully visible), with each pie divided into 4 slices. In the “easy” pie, the slices are teal (40.6%), yellow (45.9%), orange (10.1%), and red (3.3%), with percentage labels printed inside the slices. In the “medium” pie, the slices are teal (44.6%), yellow (44.3%), orange (7.2%), and red (3.9%), again with internal percentage labels. In the rightmost pie, the slices are teal (20.1%), yellow (36.2%), orange (36.8%), and red (7.0%), with percentages shown inside. A legend appears to the right mapping the colors to category labels (partially visible, including entries such as “N−K+,” “N−K−,” and “N+K−”), and none of the slices appear exploded or otherwise visually emphasized; the slice ordering appears consistent across the pies.
